provenance.l: Apollo 15 Mission Report (Tables 3-I and 3-V, sections 3.2 to 3.4): range zero 13:34:00 GMT 1971-07-26. The direct rendezvous: ascent, TPI 172:29:40.0 (2.6 s, 72.7 ft/s on the LM guidance computer; Table 3-V prints "12.7", an OCR slip), midcourse corrections, TPF/braking 173:11:07 (no duration or delta-V in the sources read: 25 s is an estimate). Quote: "The direct rendezvous technique, first used on Apollo 14, was executed nominally". Ascent 431 s and 6,059 ft/s (OCR of Table 3-V); orbit 42.5 x 9.0 n.mi, no vernier adjustment; CSM 64.5 x 53.6 n.mi after the 165:11:33 plane change; docking 173:36:25.5; ascent stage jettison 179:30:01.4 (impact 181:29:37.0); subsatellite release 222:39:29.1 (orbit shaping 221:20:48.0, 66.4 ft/s); TEI 223:48:45.84, 140.90 s, 3,046.8 ft/s. All times are the mission report / SP-4029 clock; entry compilation figures are in the splashdown profile

NASA SP-4029 Apollo 15 timeline: GET and GMT of liftoff, docking, jettison, the SIM bay door and the subsatellite events. Apollo 15 SIM bay: door jettisoned 074:06:47.1 (MR15 Table 3-I), the bay stays on the service module to entry; the subsatellite launched from it at 222:39:29.1 into a 76.3 x 55.1 mi orbit (MR15 3.2.5)
NASA SP-4029 Apollo 15 trans-Earth phase: TEI burn duration, delta-V and flight-path angle at cutoff
